metadata.orrery:spec: # yaml-language-server: $schema=../references/diagram.schema.json title: Hub-and-spoke network with central inspection on AWS subtitle: Workload VPCs attach to a Transit Gateway that sends their internet traffic through Network Firewall in an inspection VPC; the data center joins the same hub over VPN direction: down layout: { spacing: 0.9 } legend: solid: Egress traffic, inspected dashed: Site-to-Site VPN path (both ways) groups: cloud: { type: aws:cloud } region: { type: aws:region, label: us-east-1, in: cloud } spokes: { type: aws:generic, label: Workload VPCs, in: region } vpc-a: { type: aws:vpc, label: VPC A 10.1.0.0/16, in: spokes } vpc-b: { type: aws:vpc, label: VPC B 10.2.0.0/16, in: spokes } vpc-c: { type: aws:vpc, label: VPC C 10.3.0.0/16, in: spokes } inspection: { type: aws:vpc, label: Inspection VPC, in: region } firewall-subnet: { type: aws:private-subnet, label: Private subnet (Firewall), in: inspection } public-subnet: { type: aws:public-subnet, label: Public subnet, in: inspection } dc: { type: aws:corporate-dc, label: Corporate data center } nodes: app-a: { icon: aws:ec2, label: Amazon EC2, note: Workload A, in: vpc-a } app-b: { icon: aws:ec2, label: Amazon EC2, note: Workload B, in: vpc-b } app-c: { icon: aws:ec2, label: Amazon EC2, note: Workload C, in: vpc-c } tgw: { icon: aws:transit-gateway, label: AWS Transit Gateway, note: Spoke and inspection route tables, in: region } firewall: { icon: aws:network-firewall-endpoints, label: AWS Network Firewall, note: Allows or drops each flow, in: firewall-subnet } nat: { icon: aws:vpc-nat-gateway, label: NAT gateway, in: public-subnet } igw: { icon: aws:vpc-internet-gateway, label: Internet gateway, in: inspection } vpn: { icon: aws:site-to-site-vpn, label: AWS Site-to-Site VPN, note: Two IPsec tunnels, in: region } internet: { icon: aws:internet, label: Internet } cgw: { icon: aws:vpc-customer-gateway, label: Customer gateway, note: On-premises router, in: dc } servers: { icon: aws:servers, label: Corporate servers, note: 172.16.0.0/16, in: dc } edges: - spokes -> tgw: { label: VPC attachments } # The inspection VPC's attachment is the arrow to its border, so the firewall subnet's header # has no arrow through it. - tgw -> inspection: { label: inspect } # constraint: false keeps the firewall and NAT subnets side by side; the internet gateway sits # under the NAT gateway, on the way out. - firewall -> nat: { constraint: false } - nat -> igw - igw -> internet: { label: public } - tgw --- vpn: VPN attachment - vpn --- cgw: IPsec - { from: cgw, to: servers, line: dashed, arrow: none, label: LAN, constraint: false }

svg.title: Hub-and-spoke network with central inspection on AWS
svg.desc: Hub-and-spoke network with central inspection on AWS. 11 components in 10 groups. Connections: Workload VPCs to AWS Transit Gateway (VPC attachments); AWS Transit Gateway to Inspection VPC (inspect); AWS Network Firewall to NAT gateway; NAT gateway to Internet gateway; Internet gateway to Internet (public); AWS Transit Gateway to AWS Site-to-Site VPN (VPN attachment); AWS Site-to-Site VPN to Customer gateway (IPsec); Customer gateway to Corporate servers (LAN).
